author: Mark Atwood
text:
## Crypto-security 2nd pass — confidence calibration (2026-05-17)

This is the 2nd crypto-security supplement pass against JMAP-x2gd. The 1st pass landed on 2026-05-16 (findings .91–.97) with a ~12% miss-a-P0 calibration. Twenty-eight commits landed on crate-jmap-chat-server since fca0c74; several explicitly targeted the 1st pass's findings.

### Findings filed this pass

- JMAP-x2gd.107 (P3 / crypto-security): overQuota descriptions back-channel per-Space counts AND deployment cap values to any caller with /set permission. Workspace AGENTS.md 'Backend caps and limits' is explicit that caps are NOT spec-mandated and should NOT be cap-advertising — the JMAP Quota extension is the right surface. Two sites: memory.rs:2792 (backend-canonical from 8853c54) and space.rs:849 (handler defense-in-depth from earlier).
- JMAP-x2gd.108 (P3 / crypto-security): invite.rs:258-259 source comment claims the default generate_invite_code is nanosecond-seeded and not CSPRNG — stale wording inherited from the pre-sc1b.78 era. The trait has no default impl; the reference MemoryBackend is CSPRNG (getrandom::fill, 128 bits, hex). Risk is purely developer-trust / handler-author misinterpretation.

### Status of prior findings (.91–.97)

- .91 (P1, backend Display leak at chat.rs:332 + message.rs:853) — **CLOSED** by fde0db0 (chat.rs:332) and 23a9a32 (message.rs:858) per beads close-reason. Burn-on-read canary added in eb699e4. Duplicate-Direct cleanup canary split out as .102 (open).
- .92 (P2, parse_structural_entries Vec::with_capacity(arr.len())) — still OPEN, fix not yet landed; site is identical at space.rs:139.
- .93 (P2, Id::from unchecked) — still OPEN, workspace-canonical drift pending the canonical mail-server fix first.
- .94 (P2, generate_invite_code rustdoc silent on storage discipline) — still OPEN; trait rustdoc covers length / entropy / encoding / lifespan / ct_eq but not at-rest storage.
- .95 (P3, inviteCode .to_owned() with no length cap at space.rs:1436) — still OPEN; site is structurally unchanged.
- .96 (P3, MemoryBackend SetError descriptions interpolate serde_json::Error verbatim into wire output) — still OPEN; same 8 sites in chat-server's memory.rs. Confirmed: this is chat-server-specific drift, NOT workspace-canonical (mail-server's memory.rs wraps every serde error as MemoryError → BackendSetError::Other → server_fail_from_backend redaction). One adjacent analog in metadata-server (metadata-server/src/memory.rs:1159) but not workspace-wide.
- .97 (P3, SpaceInvite Debug derive leaks code) — **effectively closed** by a manual Debug impl at chat-types/src/space.rs:227-242 + space_invite_debug_does_not_leak_code canary test at line 446. The beads issue itself is still OPEN status — recommend explicit close. The fix landed in the chat-types crate, not chat-server, so the supplemental tracker likely missed the discovery.

### Sections covered vs skipped

- **Section A (key material lifecycle):** spent ~25 minutes. SpaceInvite.code is the only credential-grade type in chat-server's surface; redaction landed; ct_eq used at compare. Read all relevant code paths (backend.rs trait doc, space.rs handler, invite.rs create path, memory.rs reference impl, tests/common/mod.rs harness). No new types of concern introduced.
- **Section B (side-channel hygiene):** spent ~15 minutes. ct_eq at space.rs:1482 verified. `.find(|inv| inv.code.ct_eq(...))` leaks ordering through iteration timing, but this is the standard table-lookup pattern and is generally accepted (the alternative — iterate every entry unconditionally and OR the matches — is not what this code does). No filing because hardening tradeoff is documented and the leak channel is mild.
- **Section C (untrusted input at protocol boundaries):** spent ~25 minutes including the cap-check arithmetic audit. .92 + .93 + .95 cover the headline boundaries from the 1st pass; verified they are unchanged by the 28 commits. New cap-check code uses saturating_add and bounded u32 conversions — sound. The space.rs:1283 metadata-patch deserialize-error description interpolation was NOT filed because the deserialized type (SpaceMetadataPatch) is a public wire type whose field names are spec-public, unlike .96's case (internal Category / SpaceRole types).
- **Section D (random source quality):** spent ~10 minutes. getrandom::fill is the only CSPRNG consumer; documented well. .108 covers the source-comment confusion. No additional findings.
- **Section E (persistent storage of secrets):** spent ~5 minutes. .94 still covers the storage-discipline trait gap; nothing new at this layer.
- **Section F (logging output safety):** spent ~10 minutes. Verified zero tracing!/log!/println! emissions in src/ and tests/common/. Workspace 'Security testing' pattern 2 (log-capture canary) is N/A for chat-server because there are no log emissions to canary. Pattern 1 (Debug-redaction canary) landed in chat-types per .97 effective-close.
- **Section G (algorithm and parameter choice):** spent ~5 minutes. 128-bit CSPRNG → 32-char hex. ct_eq. No other primitives. No findings.

### Probability of missed P0

**~10% chance a competent third-party crypto reviewer would find a P0 I did not flag.**

Slightly lower than the 1st pass's ~12% because:
1. The 28-commit surface this pass had to scan was much smaller than the original epic surface, and most commits were either rustdoc, refactor, or directly closed prior findings.
2. The 1st pass's framing was right on the heavy-credential-handling sites (invite codes, redaction); the 2nd pass's diff confirmed no new credential-grade surface landed.
3. The b2ab031 Space/join idempotent-rewrite is a behavioral change in a security-relevant code path (TOCTOU); I verified the dedup semantics but did NOT independently exercise a multi-account stress test or model-check the race state space. JMAP-x2gd.2 (P0) already tracks the broader race; the b2ab031 fix narrows but does not close it.
4. The cap-check arithmetic in 8853c54 uses saturating_add and u32::try_from — safe by construction; .107 is information-disclosure, not arithmetic.

### Least confident findings (downgrade-on-pushback list)

- **.107 (overQuota cap leak)** — I'd downgrade to opinion if a workspace policy debate concluded that overQuota descriptions are explicitly acceptable surface for cap-bearing detail (e.g. "clients need to know which retry size is feasible"). The AGENTS.md backend-caps-and-limits §explicitly contradicts that read, but a policy-revision call could land. P3 is already the floor; opinion is one rung down. Most plausibly someone pushes back "every JMAP server in production names the cap in the error" — that's true at the RFC 8620 §5.3 level (overQuota IS the error type) but is silent on the description content.
- **.108 (stale invite.rs comment)** — pure hygiene; opinion-rung absolutely arguable.

### Uncertainty sources

1. I did NOT spawn an explore subagent for the workspace-wide subtle / getrandom audit because grep was fast and complete; if there is a credential-grade type in a sibling crate that doesn't use either dep yet, I would not have found it. Mitigation: confirmed jmap-cid-types and jmap-base-client use both deps as expected; jmap-testjig uses subtle for bearer token compare.
2. I did NOT inspect the 21+ test files under crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/ for fixture leaks (canary literals appearing in committed fixtures). Sampled tests/integration.rs and tests/common/mod.rs only.
3. The b2ab031 dedup-on-TOCTOU correctness is not independently model-checked. JMAP-x2gd.2 already escalates this domain.
4. .96 (.107's structural cousin) was NOT re-verified site-by-site because the 8 line numbers in the original finding may be off-by-handful after intervening edits. Confirmed the pattern still exists at the same shape; exact line numbers may need a re-anchor before fix lands.

### Conditions that would raise confidence above ~10%

1. Tracing-style log-capture canary added to the kit (currently N/A because no log emissions) as a tripwire for future contributor-added log calls.
2. The .107 fix landing with an integration test asserting absence of cap/count substrings in overQuota descriptions (parallel to the burn-on-read canary at eb699e4).
3. A modelling pass on Space/join → invite-uses increment under concurrent same-invite redemption from multiple accounts; .92 + .93 + .95 + .2 are all interacting in that code path.

### Trigger for deeper-pass P1

10% is below the 20% threshold, so a deeper-pass / external-review P1 bead is NOT filed this pass. If the .107 review surfaces a workspace-wide overQuota policy debate, that's where the next pass would start.
